definition.name: apply_patch
definition.description:
Change workspace files in exactly one of three forms. patch: a bounded UTF-8 git-style unified diff or a Codex *** Begin Patch envelope, applied after exact all-file preflight; Codex Update File accepts an optional *** Move to: destination immediately after its header, with or without content hunks; the destination must not exist. All-file preflight precedes per-file publication without rollback; publication failure requires recovery. Git-style rename, binary, copy, and mode-only patches are rejected. file_path with old_string, new_string and optional replace_all: one exact replacement (an empty old_string creates the file, or overwrites it with replace_all). file_path with edits: every edits[].old_string non-empty, unique in the original file and non-overlapping; all apply together or none does. The forms do not combine. Success returns changed_files=N followed by A/M/D and each JSON-quoted workspace-relative changed path in lexical order; moves list both paths and unchanged files are omitted. Empty old_string with replace_all requires an explicit text read of an existing file in this session attachment and unchanged content, not just unchanged mtime. Read again after each change to that file or resume/reload; context-checked patches need no prior read.

Modify example:
diff --git a/old.txt b/old.txt
--- a/old.txt
+++ b/old.txt
@@ -1 +1 @@
-before
+after

Create example:
diff --git a/new.txt b/new.txt
new file mode 100644
--- /dev/null
+++ b/new.txt
@@ -0,0 +1 @@
+created

Prefer one small successful patch over many retries.

definition.name: list_agents
definition.description: List visible agents with description and prompt_bytes, not prompt text. inbox[] includes only unread messages addressed to you; include_read=true adds the newest 64 acknowledged messages per recipient, newest first. Acknowledged rows carry message_id, from, purpose, priority, in_reply_to, body_bytes and a 160-byte body preview; unread rows carry body_bytes and previews capped at 2048 bytes; full model-authored bodies (up to 16384 bytes) reach session delivery and a parent's await. Result notices carry output_bytes and output_truncated; parents await the child for the full output. Send purpose=reply with in_reply_to set to inbox[].message_id. Sealed rows name candidate_commit and candidate_base; compare those immutable snapshots to inspect the work with the checkout's VCS. Retained candidates are objects naming candidate_id, candidate_kind, source_candidate, conflict_target, conflict_paths (at most 16), resolves and adopted_via where applicable.

definition.name: merge_plan
definition.description: Replace or merge a bounded task list by item id. When merge is true (default), update matching ids; when false, replace the list. Status cancelled removes an id.

definition.description: Read bounded output from one exact process-session cursor.

definition.description: Start one canonical joined process session.

definition.name: process_session_terminate
definition.description: Terminate and join one canonical process session.

definition.name: read_file
definition.description: Read one workspace text file. path is workspace-relative or absolute inside the workspace; paths outside the workspace and `..` are refused, except exactly a path a process result or completion notice named on its `full output:` line. A `full output:` path issued by an earlier process (before a restart or reload) or another agent is refused. offset is a 1-indexed start line (default 1). limit is a maximum line count (default 200, max 2000). Returns a JSON string with content (the file text, preserving LF/CRLF and final newline), offset (1-indexed), lines, eof, and next_offset (null at EOF), plus optional workspace_generation. A page holds at most 256 KiB; continue from next_offset. A line over 2000 characters is clipped with a marker and counted in clipped_lines; invalid UTF-8 is replaced and marked lossy=true; binary files are refused. In JavaScript use JSON.parse(await tools.read_file({...})).content; in Python use json.loads(await read_file({...}))["content"]. Metadata is not file content. Check eof before treating the result as the entire file.

definition.name: search_repository
definition.description: Search regular UTF-8 files below one directory for a literal string in one bounded deterministic query. path is workspace-relative or absolute inside the workspace; paths outside the workspace and `..` are refused, except exactly a path a process result or completion notice named on its `full output:` line. A `full output:` path issued by an earlier process (before a restart or reload) or another agent is refused; an admitted one is searched whole, up to its 64 MiB bound. query is required for content search. Matching is ASCII-insensitive by default; set case_sensitive=true for exact byte matching. paths_only=true with filename_glob lists matching paths (query is still required but ignored). With use_regex, paths_only lists unique matching files and counts_only lists per-file match counts. head_limit caps returned matches (max 4096). offset skips that many matches before applying head_limit. Paths matched by .gitignore or .ignore are not searched, nor is .git; other dotfiles are. Content scans are bounded at 256 MiB and traversal at 10,000 entries; files over 1 MiB and binary files are skipped and counted. Incompleteness is reported on the first line with the bound and how to narrow path, filename_glob or query.

definition.name: send_agent_message
definition.description: Send a message to another agent. A child is already working from spawn: mail is a follow-up on its running turn (priority=urgent steers; omitted priority is urgent from a parent to its running child, deferred otherwise), not how the prompt is assigned. A finished child takes purpose=followup, which re-tasks it on a new attempt with a new turn token and, if you give one, a new output_schema_json. To re-task a child held for recovery, its direct parent may set acknowledge_recovery to its current attempt_id: this acknowledges that a tool may have changed this workspace. The host settles recovery without replaying uncertain work before admitting the fresh attempt; unresolved ownership or effect evidence still refuses. Followup merges the parent's current state into a live-fork copy when clean; refresh=false keeps its base. Copies minted over a candidate keep their pinned base. purpose=reply requires in_reply_to set to a message_id from list_agents inbox[]; in_reply_to only when purpose=reply.

definition.name: submit_result
definition.description: Submit this attempt's result. Required for every child, including supervisors; omitting it is completed_without_submission. Assistant text is not the result.

definition.name: read_file
definition.description: Read one workspace text file. path is workspace-relative or absolute inside the workspace; paths outside the workspace and `..` are refused, except exactly a path a process result or completion notice named on its `full output:` line. A `full output:` path issued by an earlier process (before a restart or reload) or another agent is refused. offset is a 1-indexed start line (default 1). limit is a maximum line count (default 200, max 2000). Returns a JSON string with content (the file text, preserving LF/CRLF and final newline), offset (1-indexed), lines, eof, and next_offset (null at EOF), plus optional workspace_generation. A page holds at most 256 KiB; continue from next_offset. A line over 2000 characters is clipped with a marker and counted in clipped_lines; invalid UTF-8 is replaced and marked lossy=true; binary files are refused. definition.name: search_repository
definition.description: Search regular UTF-8 files below one directory for a literal string in one bounded deterministic query. path is workspace-relative or absolute inside the workspace; paths outside the workspace and `..` are refused, except exactly a path a process result or completion notice named on its `full output:` line. Matching is ASCII-insensitive by default; set case_sensitive=true for exact byte matching. paths_only=true with filename_glob lists matching paths (query is still required but ignored). With use_regex, paths_only lists unique matching files and counts_only lists per-file match counts. head_limit caps returned matches (max 4096). offset skips that many matches before applying head_limit. Paths matched by .gitignore or .ignore are not searched, nor is .git; other dotfiles are. Content scans are bounded at 256 MiB and traversal at 10,000 entries; files over 1 MiB and binary files are skipped and counted. definition.name: send_agent_message

Spawn a child from a template in the working set. Required fields: template, prompt, output_schema_json, tier. The receipt is a running child with an attempt_id, not a result. Child results and questions arrive as mail; wait_agent returns them. Default: children share your checkout. Give them file-disjoint work, or run writers in sequence. Pass workspace=fork when more than one child must write at the same time, or when the work should stay off this checkout. tier is clipped to the template ceiling: read_only refuses Plak file writes; mutate allows them. Settlement is not success: output_json is present only after submit_result. Do not call send_agent_message to start it. output_schema_json is a JSON string for the child's submit_result object, like {"type":"object","properties":{"summary":{"type":"string"}},"required":["summary"]}. Caps: 32 live nodes, depth 4, 8 undelivered or active direct children; messages ≤16384 bytes; output_json ≤262144 bytes.

Spawn sub-agents only when the user asks for delegation, sub-agents, or parallel work. Requests for depth, thoroughness, or research are not that permission. When asked, actually spawn; saying you will is not delegation. Otherwise do the work yourself.

Spawn by template name only. Do not name accounts, models, or effort. Templates you may spawn:
- explore:  (tier ≤ read_only · spawns none · adopts no)
- implement:  (tier ≤ mutate · spawns none · adopts no)
- orchestrate:  (tier ≤ read_only · spawns review, explore, implement · adopts yes)
- review:  (tier ≤ read_only · spawns none · adopts no)

definition.name: update_plan
definition.description: Replace the bounded task plan and return its new authoritative revision and statuses.

definition.name: wait_agent
definition.description: Wait until any watched child settles, sends a question or reply, or sends urgent mail (interrupted also settles). Deferred finding/coordinate mail does not wake; it stays unread and rides any later return. A bare wait with only non-waking mail pending returns it without parking. Omit agent_ids to watch the children that have not reported yet: each result comes back once, and no_pending_children means all have. Returns a row per watched id with its attempt status, mail[] in arrival order with full bodies and message ids of unread mail it consumed (result mail has only message_id, purpose, attempt_id when its result is in agents[]), and woke_by (settled, mail, timeout). Returned mail is acknowledged once; later waits do not wake on it again. Child results and questions arrive as mail; wait_agent returns them. A human or unwatched-parent steer returns woke_by=steer without its text; watched urgent mail still returns woke_by=mail with its body. If one of your own background processes becomes terminal after this wait starts, it returns woke_by=process with processes naming those ids; already-terminal processes do not wake it again. Process completion is reported automatically. Naming delivered and running children together waits for new mail or settlement; naming only delivered children re-reads without parking. Settlement is not success: relay output_json from rows that submitted; completed_without_submission has none. Settlement does not change your checkout. timed_out: true means none settled; call again. timeout_ms defaults to 300000, max 3600000.

definition.name: adopt_candidate
definition.description: Integrate a sealed candidate from your subtree into your own workspace by candidate_id, as working-tree changes with no commit. A forked child's edits are not in your checkout until this succeeds. A textual Git merge_conflict pins a conflict candidate without changing your checkout: spawn a resolver with workspace=fork and inputs=[conflict candidate], or explicitly pass accept_conflicts=true to land its markers. Every merge_conflict is a failed result that keeps the child copy; conflict candidates and resolvers belong only to the original adopter, and success accepts the source once. target_changed means your copy moved since expected_target. A wait_agent or list_agents row names the candidate once the child has sealed. Pass revert=true to undo this adoption's delta while preserving later edits. The receipt lists the changed files.

definition.name: apply_patch
definition.description:
Change workspace files in exactly one of three forms. patch: a bounded UTF-8 git-style unified diff or a Codex *** Begin Patch envelope, applied after exact all-file preflight; Codex Update File accepts an optional *** Move to: destination immediately after its header, with or without content hunks; the destination must not exist. All-file preflight precedes per-file publication without rollback; publication failure requires recovery. Git-style rename, binary, copy, and mode-only patches are rejected. file_path with old_string, new_string and optional replace_all: one exact replacement (an empty old_string creates the file, or overwrites it with replace_all). file_path with edits: every edits[].old_string non-empty, unique in the original file and non-overlapping; all apply together or none does. The forms do not combine. Success returns changed_files=N followed by A/M/D and each JSON-quoted workspace-relative changed path in lexical order; moves list both paths and unchanged files are omitted. Empty old_string with replace_all requires an explicit text read of an existing file in this session attachment and unchanged content, not just unchanged mtime. Read again after each change to that file or resume/reload; context-checked patches need no prior read.

Modify example:
diff --git a/old.txt b/old.txt
--- a/old.txt
+++ b/old.txt
@@ -1 +1 @@
-before
+after

Create example:
diff --git a/new.txt b/new.txt
new file mode 100644
--- /dev/null
+++ b/new.txt
@@ -0,0 +1 @@
+created

Prefer one small successful patch over many retries.

definition.name: close_agent
definition.description: End the named child and its descendants permanently; closed rows stay inspectable in list_agents.

definition.name: discard_workspace
definition.description: Drop a child fork by workspace_id, giving up its unadopted candidates and their pins without adopting anything from it.

definition.name: interrupt_agent
definition.description: Cancel the named child's current turn only; any open wait_agent returns with status interrupted; the node stays listable and can receive follow-up mail; there is no separate resume tool.

definition.name: list_agents
definition.description: List visible agents with description and prompt_bytes, not prompt text. inbox[] includes only unread messages addressed to you; include_read=true adds the newest 64 acknowledged messages per recipient, newest first. Acknowledged rows carry message_id, from, purpose, priority, in_reply_to, body_bytes and a 160-byte body preview; unread rows carry body_bytes and previews capped at 2048 bytes; full model-authored bodies (up to 16384 bytes) reach session delivery and a parent's await. Result notices carry output_bytes and output_truncated; parents await the child for the full output. Send purpose=reply with in_reply_to set to inbox[].message_id. Sealed rows name candidate_commit and candidate_base; compare those immutable snapshots to inspect the work with the checkout's VCS. Retained candidates are objects naming candidate_id, candidate_kind, source_candidate, conflict_target, conflict_paths (at most 16), resolves and adopted_via where applicable.

definition.name: process_session_poll
definition.description: Read bounded output from one exact process-session cursor.

definition.name: process_session_start
definition.description: Start one canonical joined process session.

definition.name: process_session_terminate
definition.description: Terminate and join one canonical process session.

definition.name: read_file
definition.description: Read one workspace text file. path is workspace-relative or absolute inside the workspace; paths outside the workspace and `..` are refused, except exactly a path a process result or completion notice named on its `full output:` line. A `full output:` path issued by an earlier process (before a restart or reload) or another agent is refused. offset is a 1-indexed start line (default 1). limit is a maximum line count (default 200, max 2000). Returns a JSON string with content (the file text, preserving LF/CRLF and final newline), offset (1-indexed), lines, eof, and next_offset (null at EOF), plus optional workspace_generation. A page holds at most 256 KiB; continue from next_offset. A line over 2000 characters is clipped with a marker and counted in clipped_lines; invalid UTF-8 is replaced and marked lossy=true; binary files are refused. In JavaScript use JSON.parse(await tools.read_file({...})).content; in Python use json.loads(await read_file({...}))["content"]. Metadata is not file content. Check eof before treating the result as the entire file.

definition.name: search_repository
definition.description: Search regular UTF-8 files below one directory for a literal string in one bounded deterministic query. path is workspace-relative or absolute inside the workspace; paths outside the workspace and `..` are refused, except exactly a path a process result or completion notice named on its `full output:` line. A `full output:` path issued by an earlier process (before a restart or reload) or another agent is refused; an admitted one is searched whole, up to its 64 MiB bound. query is required for content search. Matching is ASCII-insensitive by default; set case_sensitive=true for exact byte matching. paths_only=true with filename_glob lists matching paths (query is still required but ignored). With use_regex, paths_only lists unique matching files and counts_only lists per-file match counts. head_limit caps returned matches (max 4096). offset skips that many matches before applying head_limit. Paths matched by .gitignore or .ignore are not searched, nor is .git; other dotfiles are. Content scans are bounded at 256 MiB and traversal at 10,000 entries; files over 1 MiB and binary files are skipped and counted. Incompleteness is reported on the first line with the bound and how to narrow path, filename_glob or query.

definition.name: send_agent_message
definition.description: Send a message to another agent. A child is already working from spawn: mail is a follow-up on its running turn (priority=urgent steers; omitted priority is urgent from a parent to its running child, deferred otherwise), not how the prompt is assigned. A finished child takes purpose=followup, which re-tasks it on a new attempt with a new turn token and, if you give one, a new output_schema_json. To re-task a child held for recovery, its direct parent may set acknowledge_recovery to its current attempt_id: this acknowledges that a tool may have changed this workspace. The host settles recovery without replaying uncertain work before admitting the fresh attempt; unresolved ownership or effect evidence still refuses. Followup merges the parent's current state into a live-fork copy when clean; refresh=false keeps its base. Copies minted over a candidate keep their pinned base. purpose=reply requires in_reply_to set to a message_id from list_agents inbox[]; in_reply_to only when purpose=reply.

definition.name: apply_patch
definition.description:
Change workspace files in exactly one of three forms. patch: a bounded UTF-8 git-style unified diff or a Codex *** Begin Patch envelope, applied after exact all-file preflight; Codex Update File accepts an optional *** Move to: destination immediately after its header, with or without content hunks; the destination must not exist. All-file preflight precedes per-file publication without rollback; publication failure requires recovery. Git-style rename, binary, copy, and mode-only patches are rejected. file_path with old_string, new_string and optional replace_all: one exact replacement (an empty old_string creates the file, or overwrites it with replace_all). file_path with edits: every edits[].old_string non-empty, unique in the original file and non-overlapping; all apply together or none does. The forms do not combine. Success returns changed_files=N followed by A/M/D and each JSON-quoted workspace-relative changed path in lexical order; moves list both paths and unchanged files are omitted. Empty old_string with replace_all requires an explicit text read of an existing file in this session attachment and unchanged content, not just unchanged mtime. Read again after each change to that file or resume/reload; context-checked patches need no prior read.

Modify example:
diff --git a/old.txt b/old.txt
--- a/old.txt
+++ b/old.txt
@@ -1 +1 @@
-before
+after

Create example:
diff --git a/new.txt b/new.txt
new file mode 100644
--- /dev/null
+++ b/new.txt
@@ -0,0 +1 @@
+created

Prefer one small successful patch over many retries.

definition.name: adopt_candidate
definition.description: Integrate a sealed candidate from your subtree into your own workspace by candidate_id, as working-tree changes with no commit. A forked child's edits are not in your checkout until this succeeds. A textual Git merge_conflict pins a conflict candidate without changing your checkout: spawn a resolver with workspace=fork and inputs=[conflict candidate], or explicitly pass accept_conflicts=true to land its markers. Every merge_conflict is a failed result that keeps the child copy; conflict candidates and resolvers belong only to the original adopter, and success accepts the source once. target_changed means your copy moved since expected_target. A wait_agent or list_agents row names the candidate once the child has sealed. Pass revert=true to undo this adoption's delta while preserving later edits. The receipt lists the changed files.

accept_conflicts.description: Explicitly accept text conflict markers into your checkout. Required for a conflict candidate or an unresolved resolver.

evidence.description: Review attempt ids recorded with the adoption.

expected_target.description: Snapshot of your copy the adoption must land on; a moved copy is refused target_changed.

revert.description: Undo this adoption's delta, preserving later edits.

definition.name: close_agent
definition.description: End the named child and its descendants permanently; closed rows stay inspectable in list_agents.

expected_attempt_id.description: Refused with attempt_mismatch unless it is the child's current attempt.

definition.name: discard_workspace
definition.description: Drop a child fork by workspace_id, giving up its unadopted candidates and their pins without adopting anything from it.

definition.name: interrupt_agent
definition.description: Cancel the named child's current turn only; any open wait_agent returns with status interrupted; the node stays listable and can receive follow-up mail; there is no separate resume tool.

expected_attempt_id.description: Refused with attempt_mismatch unless it is the child's current attempt.

definition.name: list_agents

Acknowledged rows carry message_id, from, purpose, priority, in_reply_to, body_bytes and a 160-byte body preview; unread rows carry body_bytes and previews capped at 2048 bytes; full model-authored bodies (up to 16384 bytes) reach session delivery and a parent's await. Result notices carry output_bytes and output_truncated; parents await the child for the full output. Send purpose=reply with in_reply_to set to inbox[].message_id. Sealed rows name candidate_commit and candidate_base; compare those immutable snapshots to inspect the work with the checkout's VCS. Retained candidates are objects naming candidate_id, candidate_kind, source_candidate, conflict_target, conflict_paths (at most 16), resolves and adopted_via where applicable.

definition.name: send_agent_message
definition.description: Send a message to another agent. A child is already working from spawn: mail is a follow-up on its running turn (priority=urgent steers; omitted priority is urgent from a parent to its running child, deferred otherwise), not how the prompt is assigned. A finished child takes purpose=followup, which re-tasks it on a new attempt with a new turn token and, if you give one, a new output_schema_json. To re-task a child held for recovery, its direct parent may set acknowledge_recovery to its current attempt_id: this acknowledges that a tool may have changed this workspace. The host settles recovery without replaying uncertain work before admitting the fresh attempt; unresolved ownership or effect evidence still refuses. Followup merges the parent's current state into a live-fork copy when clean; refresh=false keeps its base. Copies minted over a candidate keep their pinned base. purpose=reply requires in_reply_to set to a message_id from list_agents inbox[]; in_reply_to only when purpose=reply.

acknowledge_recovery.description: Followup only, from the direct parent: the child's current attempt_id. Explicitly acknowledge that a tool may have changed this workspace. The host settles recovery without replaying uncertain work before starting a fresh attempt; ownership/effect-evidence refusals still block it.

in_reply_to.description: Omit on the first message to a child. Required only when purpose is reply.

output_schema_json.description: Optional, and only with purpose=followup: a new result schema for the new attempt. Omit to keep the schema the child already has.

priority.description: Omit for urgent from a parent to its running child; deferred otherwise.

purpose.description: Omit for coordinate. Use reply only with in_reply_to set to an existing message_id. Finished children are revivable until retired. Use followup to re-task one on a new attempt; a running child takes priority=urgent instead.

refresh.description: Followup only; merge the parent's current state into a live-fork copy when clean. False keeps its base.

definition.name: spawn_agent
definition.description:
Spawn a child from a template in the working set. Required fields: template, prompt, output_schema_json, tier. The receipt is a running child with an attempt_id, not a result. Child results and questions arrive as mail; wait_agent returns them. Default: children share your checkout. Give them file-disjoint work, or run writers in sequence. Pass workspace=fork when more than one child must write at the same time, or when the work should stay off this checkout. tier is clipped to the template ceiling: read_only refuses Plak file writes; mutate allows them. Settlement is not success: output_json is present only after submit_result. Do not call send_agent_message to start it. output_schema_json is a JSON string for the child's submit_result object, like {"type":"object","properties":{"summary":{"type":"string"}},"required":["summary"]}. Caps: 32 live nodes, depth 4, 8 undelivered or active direct children; messages ≤16384 bytes; output_json ≤262144 bytes.

Spawn sub-agents only when the user asks for delegation, sub-agents, or parallel work. Requests for depth, thoroughness, or research are not that permission. When asked, actually spawn; saying you will is not delegation. Otherwise do the work yourself.

Spawn by template name only. Do not name accounts, models, or effort. Templates you may spawn:
- explore:  (tier ≤ read_only · spawns none · adopts no)
- implement:  (tier ≤ mutate · spawns none · adopts no)
- orchestrate:  (tier ≤ read_only · spawns review, explore, implement · adopts yes)
- review:  (tier ≤ read_only · spawns none · adopts no)

description.description: Short label for the attempt; does not select bind.

inputs.description: One candidate id, from a finished child's wait or list row, to start this child's copy from instead of your current state. Requires workspace=fork: inherit has no copy of its own.

output_schema_json.description: JSON string holding the child's submit_result object schema. Property types are object, array, string, number, integer, or boolean; no $ref and no combinators.

prompt.description: Task brief for the child agent.

request_key.description: Your own key for this spawn. A repeat with the same key and the same brief returns the same child instead of spawning a second one; the same key on a different brief is refused request_key_conflict.

template.description: Template to spawn, from the cards below.

workspace.description: Omit or inherit to share your checkout. fork mints an isolated copy.

definition.name: wait_agent
definition.description: Wait until any watched child settles, sends a question or reply, or sends urgent mail (interrupted also settles). Deferred finding/coordinate mail does not wake; it stays unread and rides any later return. A bare wait with only non-waking mail pending returns it without parking. Omit agent_ids to watch the children that have not reported yet: each result comes back once, and no_pending_children means all have. Returns a row per watched id with its attempt status, mail[] in arrival order with full bodies and message ids of unread mail it consumed (result mail has only message_id, purpose, attempt_id when its result is in agents[]), and woke_by (settled, mail, timeout). Returned mail is acknowledged once; later waits do not wake on it again. Child results and questions arrive as mail; wait_agent returns them. A human or unwatched-parent steer returns woke_by=steer without its text; watched urgent mail still returns woke_by=mail with its body. Settlement is not success: relay output_json from rows that submitted; completed_without_submission has none. Settlement does not change your checkout. timed_out: true means none settled; call again. timeout_ms defaults to 300000, max 3600000.

agent_ids.description: Child ids to watch; omit for the children that have not reported yet. Returns when any of them settles, with a row per watched id.

definition.name: get_command_or_subagent_output
definition.description: Get the output and status of background commands and child agents. Pass task_ids: process ids returned by run_terminal_command (N or pN) and child agent ids. Completion is reported automatically; pass a positive timeout_ms only when this turn needs a result, clamped to 3600000 ms (1 hour). Omit timeout_ms or pass 0 for an immediate snapshot. A steer returns early without interrupting anything. Only process ids: tasks[] with each task id, output, status and exit code when done; only terminal observations consume a completion notice. Naming a child returns result, a JSON string (called from code, the object itself) with agents[] (a row per named child with its attempt status, and output_json when it submitted), mail[] (unread mail it consumed, in arrival order, acknowledged once), jobs[] (a snapshot row per named process; it consumes no completion notice), timed_out and woke_by (settled, mail, timeout, steer, process). It returns when a named child settles, sends a question/reply or urgent mail, or a named process ends. Deferred finding/coordinate mail rides any later return without waking it; a bare wait with only non-waking mail pending returns without parking. Settlement is not success: relay output_json only from rows that submitted.

definition.name: kill_command_or_subagent
definition.description: Stop a background command or interrupt a child agent by task_id. A process id (N or pN) gets SIGTERM to its process group, then SIGKILL after a 2 second grace; it succeeds if the process stopped or had already exited, and a natural exit keeps its status. A child agent id cancels that child's current turn only: it stays listable, can take follow-up mail, and is not closed; close_agent ends it.

definition.name: list_agents
definition.description: List visible agents with description and prompt_bytes, not prompt text. inbox[] includes only unread messages addressed to you; include_read=true adds the newest 64 acknowledged messages per recipient, newest first. Acknowledged rows carry message_id, from, purpose, priority, in_reply_to, body_bytes and a 160-byte body preview; unread rows carry body_bytes and previews capped at 2048 bytes; full model-authored bodies (up to 16384 bytes) reach session delivery and a parent's await. Result notices carry output_bytes and output_truncated; parents await the child for the full output. Send purpose=reply with in_reply_to set to inbox[].message_id. Sealed rows name candidate_commit and candidate_base; compare those immutable snapshots to inspect the work with the checkout's VCS. Retained candidates are objects naming candidate_id, candidate_kind, source_candidate, conflict_target, conflict_paths (at most 16), resolves and adopted_via where applicable.

definition.name: merge_plan
definition.description: Replace or merge a bounded task list by item id. When merge is true (default), update matching ids; when false, replace the list. Status cancelled removes an id.

definition.name: process_session_poll
definition.description: Read bounded output from one exact process-session cursor.

definition.name: process_session_start
definition.description: Start one canonical joined process session.

definition.name: process_session_terminate
definition.description: Terminate and join one canonical process session.

definition.name: read_file
definition.description: Read one workspace text file. path is workspace-relative or absolute inside the workspace; paths outside the workspace and `..` are refused, except exactly a path a process result or completion notice named on its `full output:` line. A `full output:` path issued by an earlier process (before a restart or reload) or another agent is refused. offset is a 1-indexed start line (default 1). limit is a maximum line count (default 200, max 2000). Returns a JSON string with content (the file text, preserving LF/CRLF and final newline), offset (1-indexed), lines, eof, and next_offset (null at EOF), plus optional workspace_generation. A page holds at most 256 KiB; continue from next_offset. A line over 2000 characters is clipped with a marker and counted in clipped_lines; invalid UTF-8 is replaced and marked lossy=true; binary files are refused. In JavaScript use JSON.parse(await tools.read_file({...})).content; in Python use json.loads(await read_file({...}))["content"]. Metadata is not file content. Check eof before treating the result as the entire file.

definition.name: search_repository
definition.description: Search regular UTF-8 files below one directory for a literal string in one bounded deterministic query. path is workspace-relative or absolute inside the workspace; paths outside the workspace and `..` are refused, except exactly a path a process result or completion notice named on its `full output:` line. A `full output:` path issued by an earlier process (before a restart or reload) or another agent is refused; an admitted one is searched whole, up to its 64 MiB bound. query is required for content search. Matching is ASCII-insensitive by default; set case_sensitive=true for exact byte matching. paths_only=true with filename_glob lists matching paths (query is still required but ignored). With use_regex, paths_only lists unique matching files and counts_only lists per-file match counts. head_limit caps returned matches (max 4096). offset skips that many matches before applying head_limit. Paths matched by .gitignore or .ignore are not searched, nor is .git; other dotfiles are. Content scans are bounded at 256 MiB and traversal at 10,000 entries; files over 1 MiB and binary files are skipped and counted. Incompleteness is reported on the first line with the bound and how to narrow path, filename_glob or query.

definition.name: send_agent_message
definition.description: Send a message to another agent. A child is already working from spawn: mail is a follow-up on its running turn (priority=urgent steers; omitted priority is urgent from a parent to its running child, deferred otherwise), not how the prompt is assigned. A finished child takes purpose=followup, which re-tasks it on a new attempt with a new turn token and, if you give one, a new output_schema_json. To re-task a child held for recovery, its direct parent may set acknowledge_recovery to its current attempt_id: this acknowledges that a tool may have changed this workspace. The host settles recovery without replaying uncertain work before admitting the fresh attempt; unresolved ownership or effect evidence still refuses. Followup merges the parent's current state into a live-fork copy when clean; refresh=false keeps its base. Copies minted over a candidate keep their pinned base. purpose=reply requires in_reply_to set to a message_id from list_agents inbox[]; in_reply_to only when purpose=reply.

definition.name: spawn_agent
definition.description:
Spawn a child from a template in the working set. Required fields: template, prompt, output_schema_json, tier. The receipt is a running child with an attempt_id, not a result. Child results and questions arrive as mail; get_command_or_subagent_output returns them. Default: children share your checkout. Give them file-disjoint work, or run writers in sequence. Pass workspace=fork when more than one child must write at the same time, or when the work should stay off this checkout. tier is clipped to the template ceiling: read_only refuses Plak file writes; mutate allows them. Settlement is not success: output_json is present only after submit_result. Do not call send_agent_message to start it. output_schema_json is a JSON string for the child's submit_result object, like {"type":"object","properties":{"summary":{"type":"string"}},"required":["summary"]}. Caps: 32 live nodes, depth 4, 8 undelivered or active direct children; messages ≤16384 bytes; output_json ≤262144 bytes.

Spawn sub-agents only when the user asks for delegation, sub-agents, or parallel work. Requests for depth, thoroughness, or research are not that permission. When asked, actually spawn; saying you will is not delegation. Otherwise do the work yourself.

Spawn by template name only. Do not name accounts, models, or effort. Templates you may spawn:
- explore:  (tier ≤ read_only · spawns none · adopts no)
- implement:  (tier ≤ mutate · spawns none · adopts no)
- orchestrate:  (tier ≤ read_only · spawns review, explore, implement · adopts yes)
- review:  (tier ≤ read_only · spawns none · adopts no)

definition.name: adopt_candidate
definition.description: Integrate a sealed candidate from your subtree into your own workspace by candidate_id, as working-tree changes with no commit. A forked child's edits are not in your checkout until this succeeds. A textual Git merge_conflict pins a conflict candidate without changing your checkout: spawn a resolver with workspace=fork and inputs=[conflict candidate], or explicitly pass accept_conflicts=true to land its markers. Every merge_conflict is a failed result that keeps the child copy; conflict candidates and resolvers belong only to the original adopter, and success accepts the source once. target_changed means your copy moved since expected_target. A get_command_or_subagent_output or list_agents row names the candidate once the child has sealed. Pass revert=true to undo this adoption's delta while preserving later edits. The receipt lists the changed files.

definition.name: apply_patch
definition.description:
Change workspace files in exactly one of three forms. patch: a bounded UTF-8 git-style unified diff or a Codex *** Begin Patch envelope, applied after exact all-file preflight; Codex Update File accepts an optional *** Move to: destination immediately after its header, with or without content hunks; the destination must not exist. All-file preflight precedes per-file publication without rollback; publication failure requires recovery. Git-style rename, binary, copy, and mode-only patches are rejected. file_path with old_string, new_string and optional replace_all: one exact replacement (an empty old_string creates the file, or overwrites it with replace_all). file_path with edits: every edits[].old_string non-empty, unique in the original file and non-overlapping; all apply together or none does. The forms do not combine. Success returns changed_files=N followed by A/M/D and each JSON-quoted workspace-relative changed path in lexical order; moves list both paths and unchanged files are omitted. Empty old_string with replace_all requires an explicit text read of an existing file in this session attachment and unchanged content, not just unchanged mtime. Read again after each change to that file or resume/reload; context-checked patches need no prior read.

Modify example:
diff --git a/old.txt b/old.txt
--- a/old.txt
+++ b/old.txt
@@ -1 +1 @@
-before
+after

Create example:
diff --git a/new.txt b/new.txt
new file mode 100644
--- /dev/null
+++ b/new.txt
@@ -0,0 +1 @@
+created

Prefer one small successful patch over many retries.

expected_attempt_id.description: Refused with attempt_mismatch unless it is the child's current attempt.

definition.name: list_agents
definition.description: List visible agents with description and prompt_bytes, not prompt text. inbox[] includes only unread messages addressed to you; include_read=true adds the newest 64 acknowledged messages per recipient, newest first. Acknowledged rows carry message_id, from, purpose, priority, in_reply_to, body_bytes and a 160-byte body preview; unread rows carry body_bytes and previews capped at 2048 bytes; full model-authored bodies (up to 16384 bytes) reach session delivery and a parent's await. Result notices carry output_bytes and output_truncated; parents await the child for the full output. Send purpose=reply with in_reply_to set to inbox[].message_id. Sealed rows name candidate_commit and candidate_base; compare those immutable snapshots to inspect the work with the checkout's VCS. Retained candidates are objects naming candidate_id, candidate_kind, source_candidate, conflict_target, conflict_paths (at most 16), resolves and adopted_via where applicable.

definition.name: send_agent_message
definition.description: Send a message to another agent. A child is already working from spawn: mail is a follow-up on its running turn (priority=urgent steers; omitted priority is urgent from a parent to its running child, deferred otherwise), not how the prompt is assigned. A finished child takes purpose=followup, which re-tasks it on a new attempt with a new turn token and, if you give one, a new output_schema_json. To re-task a child held for recovery, its direct parent may set acknowledge_recovery to its current attempt_id: this acknowledges that a tool may have changed this workspace. The host settles recovery without replaying uncertain work before admitting the fresh attempt; unresolved ownership or effect evidence still refuses. Followup merges the parent's current state into a live-fork copy when clean; refresh=false keeps its base. Copies minted over a candidate keep their pinned base. purpose=reply requires in_reply_to set to a message_id from list_agents inbox[]; in_reply_to only when purpose=reply.

acknowledge_recovery.description: Followup only, from the direct parent: the child's current attempt_id. Explicitly acknowledge that a tool may have changed this workspace. The host settles recovery without replaying uncertain work before starting a fresh attempt; ownership/effect-evidence refusals still block it.

in_reply_to.description: Omit on the first message to a child. Required only when purpose is reply.

output_schema_json.description: Optional, and only with purpose=followup: a new result schema for the new attempt. Omit to keep the schema the child already has.

priority.description: Omit for urgent from a parent to its running child; deferred otherwise.

purpose.description: Omit for coordinate. Use reply only with in_reply_to set to an existing message_id. Finished children are revivable until retired. Use followup to re-task one on a new attempt; a running child takes priority=urgent instead.

refresh.description: Followup only; merge the parent's current state into a live-fork copy when clean. False keeps its base.

definition.name: spawn_agent
definition.description:
Spawn a child from a template in the working set. Required fields: template, prompt, output_schema_json, tier. The receipt is a running child with an attempt_id, not a result. Child results and questions arrive as mail; wait_agent returns them. Default: children share your checkout. Give them file-disjoint work, or run writers in sequence. Pass workspace=fork when more than one child must write at the same time, or when the work should stay off this checkout. tier is clipped to the template ceiling: read_only refuses Plak file writes; mutate allows them. Settlement is not success: output_json is present only after submit_result. Do not call send_agent_message to start it. output_schema_json is a JSON string for the child's submit_result object, like {"type":"object","properties":{"summary":{"type":"string"}},"required":["summary"]}. Caps: 32 live nodes, depth 4, 8 undelivered or active direct children; messages ≤16384 bytes; output_json ≤262144 bytes.

Spawn by template name only. Do not name accounts, models, or effort. Templates you may spawn:
- explore:  (tier ≤ read_only · spawns none · adopts no)
- implement:  (tier ≤ mutate · spawns none · adopts no)
- orchestrate:  (tier ≤ read_only · spawns review, explore, implement · adopts yes)
- review:  (tier ≤ read_only · spawns none · adopts no)

description.description: Short label for the attempt; does not select bind.

inputs.description: One candidate id, from a finished child's wait or list row, to start this child's copy from instead of your current state. Requires workspace=fork: inherit has no copy of its own.

output_schema_json.description: JSON string holding the child's submit_result object schema. Property types are object, array, string, number, integer, or boolean; no $ref and no combinators.

prompt.description: Task brief for the child agent.

request_key.description: Your own key for this spawn. A repeat with the same key and the same brief returns the same child instead of spawning a second one; the same key on a different brief is refused request_key_conflict.

template.description: Template to spawn, from the cards below.

workspace.description: Omit or inherit to share your checkout. fork mints an isolated copy.

definition.name: wait_agent
definition.description: Wait until any watched child settles, sends a question or reply, or sends urgent mail (interrupted also settles). Deferred finding/coordinate mail does not wake; it stays unread and rides any later return. A bare wait with only non-waking mail pending returns it without parking. Omit agent_ids to watch the children that have not reported yet: each result comes back once, and no_pending_children means all have. Returns a row per watched id with its attempt status, mail[] in arrival order with full bodies and message ids of unread mail it consumed (result mail has only message_id, purpose, attempt_id when its result is in agents[]), and woke_by (settled, mail, timeout). Returned mail is acknowledged once; later waits do not wake on it again. Child results and questions arrive as mail; wait_agent returns them. A human or unwatched-parent steer returns woke_by=steer without its text; watched urgent mail still returns woke_by=mail with its body. If one of your own background processes becomes terminal after this wait starts, it returns woke_by=process with processes naming those ids; already-terminal processes do not wake it again. Process completion is reported automatically. Naming delivered and running children together waits for new mail or settlement; naming only delivered children re-reads without parking. Settlement is not success: relay output_json from rows that submitted; completed_without_submission has none. Settlement does not change your checkout. timed_out: true means none settled; call again. timeout_ms defaults to 300000, max 3600000.

agent_ids.description: Child ids to watch; omit for the children that have not reported yet. Returns when any of them settles, with a row per watched id.

Paths obey workspace policy. All-file preflight precedes per-file publication without rollback. Success: changed_files=N then A/M/D and each JSON-quoted relative changed path in lexical order; moves list both paths, unchanged files are omitted.

definition.name: apply_patch
definition.description:
Change workspace files in exactly one of three forms. patch: a bounded UTF-8 git-style unified diff or a Codex *** Begin Patch envelope, applied after exact all-file preflight; Codex Update File accepts an optional *** Move to: destination immediately after its header, with or without content hunks; the destination must not exist. All-file preflight precedes per-file publication without rollback; publication failure requires recovery. Git-style rename, binary, copy, and mode-only patches are rejected. file_path with old_string, new_string and optional replace_all: one exact replacement (an empty old_string creates the file, or overwrites it with replace_all). file_path with edits: every edits[].old_string non-empty, unique in the original file and non-overlapping; all apply together or none does. The forms do not combine. Success returns changed_files=N followed by A/M/D and each JSON-quoted workspace-relative changed path in lexical order; moves list both paths and unchanged files are omitted. Empty old_string with replace_all requires an explicit text read of an existing file in this session attachment and unchanged content, not just unchanged mtime. Read again after each change to that file or resume/reload; context-checked patches need no prior read.

Modify example:
diff --git a/old.txt b/old.txt
--- a/old.txt
+++ b/old.txt
@@ -1 +1 @@
-before
+after

Create example:
diff --git a/new.txt b/new.txt
new file mode 100644
--- /dev/null
+++ b/new.txt
@@ -0,0 +1 @@
+created

Prefer one small successful patch over many retries.

definition.name: read_file
definition.description: Read one workspace text file. path is workspace-relative or absolute inside the workspace; paths outside the workspace and `..` are refused, except exactly a path a process result or completion notice named on its `full output:` line. A `full output:` path issued by an earlier process (before a restart or reload) or another agent is refused. offset is a 1-indexed start line (default 1). limit is a maximum line count (default 200, max 2000). Returns a JSON string with content (the file text, preserving LF/CRLF and final newline), offset (1-indexed), lines, eof, and next_offset (null at EOF), plus optional workspace_generation. A page holds at most 256 KiB; continue from next_offset. A line over 2000 characters is clipped with a marker and counted in clipped_lines; invalid UTF-8 is replaced and marked lossy=true; binary files are refused. In JavaScript use JSON.parse(await tools.read_file({...})).content; in Python use json.loads(await read_file({...}))["content"]. Metadata is not file content. Check eof before treating the result as the entire file.

definition.name: apply_patch
definition.description:
Change workspace files in exactly one of three forms. patch: a bounded UTF-8 git-style unified diff or a Codex *** Begin Patch envelope, applied after exact all-file preflight; Codex Update File accepts an optional *** Move to: destination immediately after its header, with or without content hunks; the destination must not exist. All-file preflight precedes per-file publication without rollback; publication failure requires recovery. Git-style rename, binary, copy, and mode-only patches are rejected. file_path with old_string, new_string and optional replace_all: one exact replacement (an empty old_string creates the file, or overwrites it with replace_all). file_path with edits: every edits[].old_string non-empty, unique in the original file and non-overlapping; all apply together or none does. The forms do not combine. Success returns changed_files=N followed by A/M/D and each JSON-quoted workspace-relative changed path in lexical order; moves list both paths and unchanged files are omitted. Empty old_string with replace_all requires an explicit text read of an existing file in this session attachment and unchanged content, not just unchanged mtime. Read again after each change to that file or resume/reload; context-checked patches need no prior read.

Modify example:
diff --git a/old.txt b/old.txt
--- a/old.txt
+++ b/old.txt
@@ -1 +1 @@
-before
+after

Create example:
diff --git a/new.txt b/new.txt
new file mode 100644
--- /dev/null
+++ b/new.txt
@@ -0,0 +1 @@
+created

Prefer one small successful patch over many retries.

A page holds at most 256 KiB; continue from next_offset. A line over 2000 characters is clipped with a marker and counted in clipped_lines; invalid UTF-8 is replaced and marked lossy=true; binary files are refused. definition.name: list_agents
definition.description: List visible agents with description and prompt_bytes, not prompt text. inbox[] includes only unread messages addressed to you; include_read=true adds the newest 64 acknowledged messages per recipient, newest first. Acknowledged rows carry message_id, from, purpose, priority, in_reply_to, body_bytes and a 160-byte body preview; unread rows carry body_bytes and previews capped at 2048 bytes; full model-authored bodies (up to 16384 bytes) reach session delivery and a parent's await. Result notices carry output_bytes and output_truncated; parents await the child for the full output. Send purpose=reply with in_reply_to set to inbox[].message_id. Sealed rows name candidate_commit and candidate_base; compare those immutable snapshots to inspect the work with the checkout's VCS. Retained candidates are objects naming candidate_id, candidate_kind, source_candidate, conflict_target, conflict_paths (at most 16), resolves and adopted_via where applicable.

definition.name: send_agent_message
definition.description: Send a message to another agent. A child is already working from spawn: mail is a follow-up on its running turn (priority=urgent steers; omitted priority is urgent from a parent to its running child, deferred otherwise), not how the prompt is assigned. A finished child takes purpose=followup, which re-tasks it on a new attempt with a new turn token and, if you give one, a new output_schema_json. To re-task a child held for recovery, its direct parent may set acknowledge_recovery to its current attempt_id: this acknowledges that a tool may have changed this workspace. The host settles recovery without replaying uncertain work before admitting the fresh attempt; unresolved ownership or effect evidence still refuses. Followup merges the parent's current state into a live-fork copy when clean; refresh=false keeps its base. Copies minted over a candidate keep their pinned base. purpose=reply requires in_reply_to set to a message_id from list_agents inbox[]; in_reply_to only when purpose=reply.

acknowledge_recovery.description: Followup only, from the direct parent: the child's current attempt_id. Explicitly acknowledge that a tool may have changed this workspace. The host settles recovery without replaying uncertain work before starting a fresh attempt; ownership/effect-evidence refusals still block it.

in_reply_to.description: Omit on the first message to a child. Required only when purpose is reply.

output_schema_json.description: Optional, and only with purpose=followup: a new result schema for the new attempt. Omit to keep the schema the child already has.

priority.description: Omit for urgent from a parent to its running child; deferred otherwise.

purpose.description: Omit for coordinate. Use reply only with in_reply_to set to an existing message_id. Finished children are revivable until retired. Use followup to re-task one on a new attempt; a running child takes priority=urgent instead.

refresh.description: Followup only; merge the parent's current state into a live-fork copy when clean. False keeps its base.

definition.name: wait_agent
definition.description: Wait until any watched child settles, sends a question or reply, or sends urgent mail (interrupted also settles). Deferred finding/coordinate mail does not wake; it stays unread and rides any later return. A bare wait with only non-waking mail pending returns it without parking. Omit agent_ids to watch the children that have not reported yet: each result comes back once, and no_pending_children means all have. Returns a row per watched id with its attempt status, mail[] in arrival order with full bodies and message ids of unread mail it consumed (result mail has only message_id, purpose, attempt_id when its result is in agents[]), and woke_by (settled, mail, timeout). Returned mail is acknowledged once; later waits do not wake on it again. Child results and questions arrive as mail; wait_agent returns them. A human or unwatched-parent steer returns woke_by=steer without its text; watched urgent mail still returns woke_by=mail with its body. If one of your own background processes becomes terminal after this wait starts, it returns woke_by=process with processes naming those ids; already-terminal processes do not wake it again. Process completion is reported automatically. Naming delivered and running children together waits for new mail or settlement; naming only delivered children re-reads without parking. Settlement is not success: relay output_json from rows that submitted; completed_without_submission has none. Settlement does not change your checkout. timed_out: true means none settled; call again. timeout_ms defaults to 300000, max 3600000.

agent_ids.description: Child ids to watch; omit for the children that have not reported yet. Returns when any of them settles, with a row per watched id.

definition.name: interrupt_agent
definition.description: Cancel the named child's current turn only; any open wait_agent returns with status interrupted; the node stays listable and can receive follow-up mail; there is no separate resume tool.

expected_attempt_id.description: Refused with attempt_mismatch unless it is the child's current attempt.

definition.name: close_agent
definition.description: End the named child and its descendants permanently; closed rows stay inspectable in list_agents.

expected_attempt_id.description: Refused with attempt_mismatch unless it is the child's current attempt.

definition.name: adopt_candidate
definition.description: Integrate a sealed candidate from your subtree into your own workspace by candidate_id, as working-tree changes with no commit. A forked child's edits are not in your checkout until this succeeds. A textual Git merge_conflict pins a conflict candidate without changing your checkout: spawn a resolver with workspace=fork and inputs=[conflict candidate], or explicitly pass accept_conflicts=true to land its markers. Every merge_conflict is a failed result that keeps the child copy; conflict candidates and resolvers belong only to the original adopter, and success accepts the source once. target_changed means your copy moved since expected_target. A wait_agent or list_agents row names the candidate once the child has sealed. Pass revert=true to undo this adoption's delta while preserving later edits. The receipt lists the changed files.

accept_conflicts.description: Explicitly accept text conflict markers into your checkout. Required for a conflict candidate or an unresolved resolver.

evidence.description: Review attempt ids recorded with the adoption.

expected_target.description: Snapshot of your copy the adoption must land on; a moved copy is refused target_changed.

revert.description: Undo this adoption's delta, preserving later edits.

definition.name: discard_workspace
definition.description: Drop a child fork by workspace_id, giving up its unadopted candidates and their pins without adopting anything from it.

definition.name: view_image
definition.description: View a local image file from the filesystem when visual inspection is needed. Use this for images already available on disk. path is an absolute path under the workspace root or a workspace-relative path without `..`; other paths are refused. PNG, JPEG, GIF and WebP are returned as an image. A model that does not accept image input is refused with the route and model named.

path.description: Local filesystem path to an image file.

definition.name: patch_envelope
definition.description: Supply a raw *** Begin Patch envelope, not JSON. Update File allows *** Move to: path after its header, with optional hunks; destination must be absent. Paths obey workspace policy. All-file preflight precedes per-file publication without rollback. Success: changed_files=N then A/M/D and each JSON-quoted relative changed path in lexical order; moves list both paths, unchanged files are omitted.

definition.name: process_session_start
definition.description: Start one canonical joined process session.

definition.name: process_session_write
definition.description: Write bounded input to one canonical joined process session.

definition.name: process_session_poll
definition.description: Read bounded output from one exact process-session cursor.

definition.name: update_plan
definition.description: Replace the bounded task plan and return its new authoritative revision and statuses.

definition.name: spawn_agent
definition.description:
Spawn a child from a template in the working set. Required fields: template, prompt, output_schema_json, tier. The receipt is a running child with an attempt_id, not a result. Child results and questions arrive as mail; wait_agent returns them. Default: children share your checkout. Give them file-disjoint work, or run writers in sequence. Pass workspace=fork when more than one child must write at the same time, or when the work should stay off this checkout. tier is clipped to the template ceiling: read_only refuses Plak file writes; mutate allows them. Settlement is not success: output_json is present only after submit_result. Do not call send_agent_message to start it. output_schema_json is a JSON string for the child's submit_result object, like {"type":"object","properties":{"summary":{"type":"string"}},"required":["summary"]}. Caps: 32 live nodes, depth 4, 8 undelivered or active direct children; messages ≤16384 bytes; output_json ≤262144 bytes.

Spawn sub-agents only when the user asks for delegation, sub-agents, or parallel work. Requests for depth, thoroughness, or research are not that permission. When asked, actually spawn; saying you will is not delegation. Otherwise do the work yourself.

Spawn by template name only. Do not name accounts, models, or effort. Templates you may spawn:
- explore:  (tier ≤ read_only · spawns none · adopts no)
- implement:  (tier ≤ mutate · spawns none · adopts no)
- orchestrate:  (tier ≤ read_only · spawns review, explore, implement · adopts yes)
- review:  (tier ≤ read_only · spawns none · adopts no)

description.description: Short label for the attempt; does not select bind.

inputs.description: One candidate id, from a finished child's wait or list row, to start this child's copy from instead of your current state. Requires workspace=fork: inherit has no copy of its own.

output_schema_json.description: JSON string holding the child's submit_result object schema. Property types are object, array, string, number, integer, or boolean; no $ref and no combinators.

prompt.description: Task brief for the child agent.

request_key.description: Your own key for this spawn. A repeat with the same key and the same brief returns the same child instead of spawning a second one; the same key on a different brief is refused request_key_conflict.

definition.name: apply_patch
definition.description:
Change workspace files in exactly one of three forms. patch: a bounded UTF-8 git-style unified diff or a Codex *** Begin Patch envelope, applied after exact all-file preflight; Codex Update File accepts an optional *** Move to: destination immediately after its header, with or without content hunks; the destination must not exist. All-file preflight precedes per-file publication without rollback; publication failure requires recovery. Git-style rename, binary, copy, and mode-only patches are rejected. file_path with old_string, new_string and optional replace_all: one exact replacement (an empty old_string creates the file, or overwrites it with replace_all). file_path with edits: every edits[].old_string non-empty, unique in the original file and non-overlapping; all apply together or none does. The forms do not combine. Success returns changed_files=N followed by A/M/D and each JSON-quoted workspace-relative changed path in lexical order; moves list both paths and unchanged files are omitted. Empty old_string with replace_all requires an explicit text read of an existing file in this session attachment and unchanged content, not just unchanged mtime. Read again after each change to that file or resume/reload; context-checked patches need no prior read.

Modify example:
diff --git a/old.txt b/old.txt
--- a/old.txt
+++ b/old.txt
@@ -1 +1 @@
-before
+after

Create example:
diff --git a/new.txt b/new.txt
new file mode 100644
--- /dev/null
+++ b/new.txt
@@ -0,0 +1 @@
+created

Prefer one small successful patch over many retries.

definition.name: inspect_image
definition.description: Inspect and return a PNG, JPEG, GIF, or WebP from the configured workspace, bounded to 196608 bytes.

definition.name: read_file
definition.description: Read one workspace text file. path is workspace-relative or absolute inside the workspace; paths outside the workspace and `..` are refused, except exactly a path a process result or completion notice named on its `full output:` line. A `full output:` path issued by an earlier process (before a restart or reload) or another agent is refused. offset is a 1-indexed start line (default 1). limit is a maximum line count (default 200, max 2000). Returns a JSON string with content (the file text, preserving LF/CRLF and final newline), offset (1-indexed), lines, eof, and next_offset (null at EOF), plus optional workspace_generation. A page holds at most 256 KiB; continue from next_offset. A line over 2000 characters is clipped with a marker and counted in clipped_lines; invalid UTF-8 is replaced and marked lossy=true; binary files are refused. In JavaScript use JSON.parse(await tools.read_file({...})).content; in Python use json.loads(await read_file({...}))["content"]. Metadata is not file content. Check eof before treating the result as the entire file.

definition.name: search_repository
definition.description: Search regular UTF-8 files below one directory for a literal string in one bounded deterministic query. path is workspace-relative or absolute inside the workspace; paths outside the workspace and `..` are refused, except exactly a path a process result or completion notice named on its `full output:` line. A `full output:` path issued by an earlier process (before a restart or reload) or another agent is refused; an admitted one is searched whole, up to its 64 MiB bound. query is required for content search. Matching is ASCII-insensitive by default; set case_sensitive=true for exact byte matching. paths_only=true with filename_glob lists matching paths (query is still required but ignored). With use_regex, paths_only lists unique matching files and counts_only lists per-file match counts. head_limit caps returned matches (max 4096). offset skips that many matches before applying head_limit. Paths matched by .gitignore or .ignore are not searched, nor is .git; other dotfiles are. Content scans are bounded at 256 MiB and traversal at 10,000 entries; files over 1 MiB and binary files are skipped and counted. Incompleteness is reported on the first line with the bound and how to narrow path, filename_glob or query.

Use this for images already available on disk. path is an absolute path under the workspace root or a workspace-relative path without `..`; other paths are refused. PNG, JPEG, GIF and WebP are returned as an image. A model that does not accept image input is refused with the route and model named.

path.description: Local filesystem path to an image file.

definition.name: list_agents
definition.description: List visible agents with description and prompt_bytes, not prompt text. inbox[] includes only unread messages addressed to you; include_read=true adds the newest 64 acknowledged messages per recipient, newest first. Acknowledged rows carry message_id, from, purpose, priority, in_reply_to, body_bytes and a 160-byte body preview; unread rows carry body_bytes and previews capped at 2048 bytes; full model-authored bodies (up to 16384 bytes) reach session delivery and a parent's await. Result notices carry output_bytes and output_truncated; parents await the child for the full output. Send purpose=reply with in_reply_to set to inbox[].message_id. Sealed rows name candidate_commit and candidate_base; compare those immutable snapshots to inspect the work with the checkout's VCS. Retained candidates are objects naming candidate_id, candidate_kind, source_candidate, conflict_target, conflict_paths (at most 16), resolves and adopted_via where applicable.

definition.name: patch_envelope
definition.description: Supply a raw *** Begin Patch envelope, not JSON. Update File allows *** Move to: path after its header, with optional hunks; destination must be absent. Paths obey workspace policy. All-file preflight precedes per-file publication without rollback. Success: changed_files=N then A/M/D and each JSON-quoted relative changed path in lexical order; moves list both paths, unchanged files are omitted.

definition.name: send_agent_message
definition.description: Send a message to another agent. A child is already working from spawn: mail is a follow-up on its running turn (priority=urgent steers; omitted priority is urgent from a parent to its running child, deferred otherwise), not how the prompt is assigned. A finished child takes purpose=followup, which re-tasks it on a new attempt with a new turn token and, if you give one, a new output_schema_json. To re-task a child held for recovery, its direct parent may set acknowledge_recovery to its current attempt_id: this acknowledges that a tool may have changed this workspace. The host settles recovery without replaying uncertain work before admitting the fresh attempt; unresolved ownership or effect evidence still refuses. Followup merges the parent's current state into a live-fork copy when clean; refresh=false keeps its base. Copies minted over a candidate keep their pinned base. purpose=reply requires in_reply_to set to a message_id from list_agents inbox[]; in_reply_to only when purpose=reply.

acknowledge_recovery.description: Followup only, from the direct parent: the child's current attempt_id. Explicitly acknowledge that a tool may have changed this workspace. The host settles recovery without replaying uncertain work before starting a fresh attempt; ownership/effect-evidence refusals still block it.

in_reply_to.description: Omit on the first message to a child. Required only when purpose is reply.

output_schema_json.description: Optional, and only with purpose=followup: a new result schema for the new attempt. Omit to keep the schema the child already has.

priority.description: Omit for urgent from a parent to its running child; deferred otherwise.

purpose.description: Omit for coordinate. Use reply only with in_reply_to set to an existing message_id. Finished children are revivable until retired. Use followup to re-task one on a new attempt; a running child takes priority=urgent instead.

refresh.description: Followup only; merge the parent's current state into a live-fork copy when clean. False keeps its base.

definition.name: apply_patch
definition.description:
Change workspace files in exactly one of three forms. patch: a bounded UTF-8 git-style unified diff or a Codex *** Begin Patch envelope, applied after exact all-file preflight; Codex Update File accepts an optional *** Move to: destination immediately after its header, with or without content hunks; the destination must not exist. All-file preflight precedes per-file publication without rollback; publication failure requires recovery. Git-style rename, binary, copy, and mode-only patches are rejected. file_path with old_string, new_string and optional replace_all: one exact replacement (an empty old_string creates the file, or overwrites it with replace_all). file_path with edits: every edits[].old_string non-empty, unique in the original file and non-overlapping; all apply together or none does. The forms do not combine. Success returns changed_files=N followed by A/M/D and each JSON-quoted workspace-relative changed path in lexical order; moves list both paths and unchanged files are omitted. Empty old_string with replace_all requires an explicit text read of an existing file in this session attachment and unchanged content, not just unchanged mtime. Read again after each change to that file or resume/reload; context-checked patches need no prior read.

Modify example:
diff --git a/old.txt b/old.txt
--- a/old.txt
+++ b/old.txt
@@ -1 +1 @@
-before
+after

Create example:
diff --git a/new.txt b/new.txt
new file mode 100644
--- /dev/null
+++ b/new.txt
@@ -0,0 +1 @@
+created

Prefer one small successful patch over many retries.

definition.name: read_file
definition.description: Read one workspace text file. path is workspace-relative or absolute inside the workspace; paths outside the workspace and `..` are refused, except exactly a path a process result or completion notice named on its `full output:` line. Incompleteness is reported on the first line with the bound and how to narrow path, filename_glob or query.

Empty old_string with replace_all requires an explicit text read of an existing file in this session attachment and unchanged content, not just unchanged mtime. Read again after each change to that file or resume/reload; context-checked patches need no prior read.

Modify example:
diff --git a/old.txt b/old.txt
--- a/old.txt
+++ b/old.txt
@@ -1 +1 @@
-before
+after

Create example:
diff --git a/new.txt b/new.txt
new file mode 100644
--- /dev/null
+++ b/new.txt
@@ -0,0 +1 @@
+created

Prefer one small successful patch over many retries.

definition.name: inspect_image
definition.description: Inspect and return a PNG, JPEG, GIF, or WebP from the configured workspace, bounded to 196608 bytes.

definition.name: read_file
definition.description: Read one workspace text file. path is workspace-relative or absolute inside the workspace; paths outside the workspace and `..` are refused, except exactly a path a process result or completion notice named on its `full output:` line. A `full output:` path issued by an earlier process (before a restart or reload) or another agent is refused. offset is a 1-indexed start line (default 1). limit is a maximum line count (default 200, max 2000). Returns a JSON string with content (the file text, preserving LF/CRLF and final newline), offset (1-indexed), lines, eof, and next_offset (null at EOF), plus optional workspace_generation. A page holds at most 256 KiB; continue from next_offset. A line over 2000 characters is clipped with a marker and counted in clipped_lines; invalid UTF-8 is replaced and marked lossy=true; binary files are refused. In JavaScript use JSON.parse(await tools.read_file({...})).content; in Python use json.loads(await read_file({...}))["content"]. Metadata is not file content. Check eof before treating the result as the entire file.

definition.name: search_repository
definition.description: Search regular UTF-8 files below one directory for a literal string in one bounded deterministic query. path is workspace-relative or absolute inside the workspace; paths outside the workspace and `..` are refused, except exactly a path a process result or completion notice named on its `full output:` line. A `full output:` path issued by an earlier process (before a restart or reload) or another agent is refused; an admitted one is searched whole, up to its 64 MiB bound. query is required for content search. Matching is ASCII-insensitive by default; set case_sensitive=true for exact byte matching. paths_only=true with filename_glob lists matching paths (query is still required but ignored). With use_regex, paths_only lists unique matching files and counts_only lists per-file match counts. head_limit caps returned matches (max 4096). offset skips that many matches before applying head_limit. Paths matched by .gitignore or .ignore are not searched, nor is .git; other dotfiles are. Content scans are bounded at 256 MiB and traversal at 10,000 entries; files over 1 MiB and binary files are skipped and counted. Incompleteness is reported on the first line with the bound and how to narrow path, filename_glob or query.
